title: Eviction Simulation + Regional Horizon Sync
content:
Meeting: Eviction Simulation + Regional Horizon Sync
Date: 2026-12-15 10:00 PT (60m)
Attendees: Aisha (infra), Sam (fleet), Luis (capacity), Caitlyn (SRE), Ravi (serving-runtime), Maria (product, by sync)

Purpose: Walk through the results from last week's eviction trace replay, align on regional capacity horizon for the next 3 weeks (holiday spike + model release), and decide short-term mitigations that are cheap to deploy before week-of-2026-12-22.

Agenda:
- Quick recap of simulation inputs and assumptions (5m)
- Key failure modes observed in trace replay (15m)
- Regional breakdown + impact to latency SLO customers (10m)
- Proposed mitigations and cost/ops tradeoffs (20m)
- Action items and owners (10m)

Recap of simulation inputs:
- Trace: 14 days of production traffic ending 2026-12-08 (mixed hosted + dedicated).
- Node types: n1-standard for control, G5x2 (A100-equivalent) GPU pools, spot/preemptible fraction set to 28% in us-west2 and eu-central1, 40% in ap-southeast1.
- Workloads: top 5 customers by QPS + steady long-tail; heavy attention on chat-streaming workloads and long-context QPS.
- Autoscaler config used: cooldown 120s, target utilization 0.68, max-burst 15 nodes in region.

Simulation findings (high level):
- Global throughput drop: median token throughput dropped 11.8% during top-5% preemption events.
- Latency tail impact: p99 increased by 320ms on average for streaming endpoints when local preemption rates exceeded 18% in a 15m window.
- Model-specific: Llama-variant families with >8k context showed biggest sensitivity (KV cache warmup and eviction churn).
- Regional winners/losers:
  - us-west2: most resilient thanks to spare reserved capacity; observed localized thrashing when preemptible eviction cascaded into dedicated pools due to misrouted failover policy.
  - eu-central1: sustained medium pressure; ~6% of requests rerouted to fallback models causing quality regressions for 2 customers.
  - ap-southeast1: highest volatility; simulation shows 18% longer cold-start tail due to limited hot cache nodes.

Specific failure modes called out:
- Eviction storm: a 4-minute correlated preemptible eviction causes the autoscaler to spin up new nodes but the node provisioning + model pull time (~2.5m median) plus sequential KV cache warmups causes a 3–5 minute window of elevated latency.
- Routing oscillation: smart-routing policy retries between regions too aggressively (3 retries) causing amplification of load on fallback regions during partial outages.
- Cache churn for long-context models: nodes that are recycled frequently have high KV load and increased per-token compute due to re-keying overhead.

Customer impact notes:
- Two latency-SLO customers (internal alias: Finance-AI, SearchPro) would experience degraded p99 on hosted endpoints at simulated peak. Product wants an alerting rule and a short notice to customers if we plan to enable any regional fallback changes.

Mitigation options discussed (summary + ops cost estimate):
1) Short-term (minutes to hours):
   - Decrease autoscaler cooldown from 120s -> 60s for streaming-heavy pools in us-west2 (owner: Sam) – ops risk: medium; cost: marginal increase in transient nodes.
   - Reduce preemptible fraction in ap-southeast1 from 40% -> 25% for the next 3 weeks (owner: Luis) – ops risk: low; cost: additional reserved capacity charge estimated ~+$9k/week.
   - Add a routing throttle: cap cross-region retries to 1 (owner: Caitlyn) – ops risk: low; cost: negligible.
2) Mid-term (days):
   - Prewarm persistent KV-cache instances for Llama-family models in eu-central1 (owner: Ravi) – ops risk: medium; infra change + config, cost: ~6 reserved GPUs.
   - Implement smarter backoff in smart-router (exponential with jitter) (owner: Aisha) – PR exists, needs canary + rollout (linked_pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/612).
3) Longer-term (weeks):
   - Capacity hedge: procure/commit an additional 40 GPUs in us-west2 and 20 in ap-southeast1 for Jan+Feb (owner: Luis / finance approval) – cost estimate included in linked_confluence page.
   - Eviction-aware autoscaler: change decision logic to prefer short-lived scale-ups that reuse warmed nodes when possible (owner: Sam + Ravi) – larger infra project.

Decisions made in this meeting:
- Apply routing throttle immediately: cross-region retries reduced to 1. (Caitlyn to patch routing config by EOD 2026-12-16).
- Reduce ap-southeast1 preemptible fraction to 25% for a 3-week window starting 2026-12-17 (Luis to file capacity change request and confirm with partners).
- Start a 3-day canary for autoscaler cooldown reduction in us-west2 (Sam to run canary on staging then production pilot; target start 2026-12-18).
- Create an A/B test for prewarming KV cache for Llama-family models in eu-central1 (Ravi to create experiment and invite product to define success metrics).

Action items (owner / due / notes):
- Caitlyn: push routing throttle config to staging and run smoke tests (due 2026-12-16) [INFRA-2483].
- Luis: submit capacity change + cost approval for ap-southeast1 preemptible shift (due 2026-12-16).
- Sam: prepare autoscaler cooldown canary plan + rollback playbook (due 2026-12-17).
- Ravi: create prewarm A/B experiment + evaluation dashboard (due 2026-12-18).
- Aisha: add customer alerting proposal for latency-SLO customers and draft messaging (due 2026-12-17).
- Maria (product): review tradeoffs and sign off on experiment metrics for SearchPro and Finance-AI (due 2026-12-17).

Open questions / Risks:
- If we reduce cross-region retries, what is the observable hit to error rate vs user-visible latency for customers with aggressive region affinity? Need to validate with synthetic traffic.
- Cost authorization: Finance needs an explicit approval for the ap-southeast1 temporary reservation. Luis will surface to Felix (finance).
- Dark-launch complexity: prewarming will increase steady-state cost; need to define minimal warm pool sizes to keep cost acceptable.

Notes / quick logs from the eviction sim run (appendix):
- Eviction replay id: replay-2026-12-09-evict-v3
- Simulator config: keep-alive true, failover-policy=route-first-available, max-tries=3
- Observed provisioning median (region): us-west2 2m10s, eu-central1 2m40s, ap-southeast1 3m20s
- Cold-node L1 cache effectiveness: 67% after first 5 minutes, asymptotes at 84% after 20m for repeated workloads

Meeting notes: quick capture style — there will be a cleaned-up playbook derived from these notes.

References:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Eviction+Simulation+Runbook
- Jira: INFRA-2483 (routing throttle), INFRA-2490 (ap-soutible capacity change)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/612

Next sync: 2026-12-18 09:30 PT — brief status update and canary review.

Document informal log: this was captured live and is intentionally a mix of notes, estimates, and specific TODOs. If you're listed as an owner and disagree with scope/cost, ping me directly so we can adjust before the EOD deadlines.
